body.p: Claims 1-20 are currently pending in the present application, with claims 1 and 14 being written in independent form. Claim 6 has been cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer. Support for amendments made herein may be found, for instance, in the claims as originally filed and in paragraph [0067] of the original specification. Thus, no new matter has been introduced into the claims.
The Office Action indicates that the drawings have been accepted by the Examiner.
The Office Action acknowledges Applicants' foreign priority claim and the receipt of the certified copy of the priority document.
The Office Action indicates that the Information Disclosure Statement filed on August 1, 2022 has been considered.

Claims 16-20 stand objected to because of alleged informalities. Applicants acknowledge that MPEP 608.01(n)(IV) describes claim form and arrangement for dependent claims. This section of the MPEP notes that a claim which depends from a dependent claim should not be separated by a claim which does not also depend from said dependent claim. However, this section also states that "in general, applicant's

sequence should not be changed" and describes that claims are renumbered upon allowance. Accordingly, Applicants request for the claims to be renumbered, as necessary, upon allowance of the pending claims, and submit that no changes to the sequence of claims are needed at this time. In view of the foregoing, Applicants request the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw this objection.

Claims 10, 11, and 18 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which Applicants regard as the invention. This rejection has been rendered moot by the present amendments. Accordingly, Applicants request the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw this rejection.

Claims 1 and 12-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. 2016/091583 ("Saybasili") in view of U.S. 2019/0056465 ("Schnetter"). Claims 2 and 16 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili and Schnetter, and further in view of U.S. 2011/0043205 ("Graesslin"). Claims 3, 4, and 17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili and Schnetter, and further in view of U.S. 2012/0256626 ("Adalsteinsson"). Claim 5 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili and Schnetter, and further in view of U.S. 2020/0142057 ("Pendse"). Claims 6-8 and 10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili and Schnetter, and further in view of U.S. 2017/0097396 ("Harvey"). Claims 9 and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as

allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili, Schnetter, and Harvey, and further in view of U.S. 2020/0337592 ("Brada"). Claims 11 and 18 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili, Schnetter, and Harvey, and further in view of U.S. 2013/0271129 ("Kess"). Claim 19 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Saybasili, Schnetter, and Graesslin, and further in view of Pendse. Applicants traverse these rejections for the reasons below.

Claim 1 is being amended to include the subject matter of claim 6. More specifically, claim 1 is amended to recite, in part, "detecting first position data, the first position data describing a position of the transmitter of the magnetic resonance device at least one of prior to or during the magnetic resonance scan" and "stopping the magnetic resonance scan in response to the first position data indicating the position of the transmitter is more than a threshold amount different from a target position."

With respect to claim 6, the Office Action admits that "Saybasili and Schnetter do not teach detecting position data, the position data describing a position of the transmitter of the magnetic resonance device at least one of prior to or during the magnetic resonance scan." Office Action, page 8. To remedy this deficiency of Saybasili in view of Schnetter, the Office Action cites to Harvey.

Harvey describes a position parameter that is "indicative of a position of at least the portion of the subject of interest relative to the at least one radio frequency transmit antenna." Harvey, paragraph [0009]. Paragraphs [0072] and [0073] of Harvey describe an adjustment and a warning signal that are output in response to a subject being closer than a minimum distance from a magnet center bore wall. However, a magnet center bore wall is stationary and Harvey is only concerned with placement of

a patient relative to the stationary magnet bore wall. Thus, Harvey does not describe or suggest at least detecting a first position of the transmitter of the magnetic resonance device as required to meet the limitations of amended claim 1.

Further, none of Saybasili, Schnetter, nor Harvey describe "stopping the magnetic resonance scan in response to the first position data indicating the position of the transmitter is more than a threshold amount different from a target position," as recited in amended claim 1.
The Office Action also does not establish that the additional art cited by the Office remedies the above-discussed deficiencies of claim 1.

For at least the reasons above, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with regard to claim 1. Consequently, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with regard to claims 2-5, 7-13, and 15-20, at least by virtue of their dependency from claim 1.
Claim 14 is amended similarly or analogously to claim 1. For at least the reasons above with respect to claim 11, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with regard to claim 14.
Accordingly, Applicants request the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the above rejection.

In view of the above, Applicants request the allowance of all the pending claims in the present application. Additionally, it should be noted that the remarks provided herein are not intended to, nor need they, comprehensively address each and every reason for the patentability of the claims over the applied art. Accordingly, it is not contended that the claims are patentable solely on the basis of the particular elements discussed herein.
Should there be any outstanding matters that need to be resolved in the present application, the Examiner is requested to contact the undersigned at the telephone number below.
